reasons: Lake identity confirms United States v. Vaneaton as the input/canonical short case name for United States v. Jack Palmer Vaneaton.
Lake citations confirm official citation 49 F.3d 1423, court 9th Cir., date_decided 1995-03-13, year 1995, plus the listed parallel and vendor-neutral citations.
The opinion frames the issue as whether police with probable cause but no warrant could arrest Vaneaton while he stood immediately inside the open doorway.
At 1426-27, the opinion makes voluntary exposure dispositive and holds that Payton was not violated because Vaneaton voluntarily opened the door in response to a noncoercive police knock.
residual_risks: The role should not be read to cover coercive show-of-authority doorway encounters.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: For precision, qualify the shorthand as voluntary opening in response to a noncoercive knock, with no threats, force, ruse, or claim of lawful authority.

reasons: The cached opinion is a Payton doorway-arrest case involving a motel room threshold and an arrest made while the suspect stood just inside the open doorway.
Because the majority treats the doorway/public-place characterization as avoiding a Payton in-home-arrest violation, the cross-doctrine doorway-arrests role is supported.
residual_risks: The majority ultimately characterizes the exposure as public-place exposure, so this is related rather than a clean in-home-arrest rule.
